question: A careers site drew this pie of why Americans quit their jobs in 2021. Low pay looks like under a quarter. Where's the trick?
answer: In the slices: they add up to 271%. Pew let everyone who had quit tick every reason that applied, and most ticked several. So 63% named low pay, as many named no way to advance, and 57% felt disrespected. People rarely leave a job for one reason; they go when a few pile up.
move: Behind a big decision, look for the several reasons, not the one.
ask: If I left my job tomorrow, which reasons would I give, and which would I keep to myself?

scene.headline: Why Americans quit their jobs
scene.honest: Most who quit had several reasons
scene.label: Reasons for quitting in 2021
scene.found: Yes: the slices add up to 271%. Each person could tick several.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Try adding up the slices.

misses.headline: A plain title. The pie is what makes the claim.
misses.label: The reasons are real. How many could each person give?

scene.name: Several answers, one pie
scene.lesson: Slices past 100% mean people gave several answers. Read each one as a share of everyone.

source: Pew Research Center, why workers quit, 2022
reference: Parker & Horowitz, Majority of workers who quit a job in 2021 cite low pay, no opportunities for advancement, feeling disrespected, Pew Research Center, 9 March 2022
